summary:
> H2O HUNT – Find Water, Find Life is an interactive educational Mars exploration where participants become junior astronauts investigating whether water existed on Mars as frozen ice or flowing liquid in the past.
>
> From Mission Control, they explore three regions: Polar Areas with layered water-ice caps and seasonal deposits, Mid-Latitude Areas with hidden underground ice-rich deposits and glacial landforms, and Ancient Valley featuring Jezero Crater with ancient river channels and a fan-shaped river delta.
>
> Learners discover how real NASA instruments work: SHARAD radar reveals buried ice layers and underground structure, CRISM spectrometer identifies water-related minerals like clays and sulfates, and HiRISE camera provides high-resolution images of Martian surface details.
>
> After exploring all regions, they complete an Evidence Report and Mission Decision Challenge, ranking regions by research priority for future missions. A sample decision prioritizes Ancient Valley first for its potential to preserve signs of past habitability, followed by Polar Areas and Mid-Latitude Areas.
>
> Built in Canva as an interactive, clickable presentation with quizzes, navigation, and ranking activity, plus a companion Mars Outpost game demo in HTML/CSS/JS, it combines space science, scientific accuracy, ease of use, and mission-based learning to make planetary science engaging and teach how observations become evidence about another world.
